learning_objective: 🎯 You will learn how to split any sentence into two clear parts: who we are talking about and what they are doing!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Every sentence is about someone or something. The Subject is the naming part of the sentence that tells us who or what is performing the action. It is usually a noun or a pronoun!
The Predicate is the action part of the sentence! It tells us what the subject is doing or being. The predicate always contains the verb.
To find the subject, simply ask 'Who?' or 'What?' before the verb. The answer is your subject, and everything else in the sentence belongs to the predicate!

fun_activity.title: ✍️ The Match-Up Game
fun_activity.instructions: Write down 3 names of your friends as Subjects on one page, and mix them up with 3 funny actions as Predicates on another page to create silly sentences!

quick_recap: ⭐ Every complete sentence has two main parts: a Subject and a Predicate.
⭐ The Subject tells us 'who' or 'what' the sentence is about.
⭐ The Predicate contains the verb and tells us what the subject does or is.
